The spotted bat (Euderma maculatum), a Threatened species, prefers arid habitats (Long, 1965) with high cliffs and canyons (Office of Endangered Species and International Activities, 1973). Lack of such habitat on the Froject Area probably excludes this bat from the region.
None of the species of amphibians, reptiles or fish determined to occur on the Project Area is considered Endangered or Threatened (Office of Endangered Species and International Activities, 1973; 1974).
The state of Montana has no Rare or Endangered Species Act, however, there are a number of species of mammals, birds and reptiles about which the Montana Department of Fish and Game have expressed concern (Flath, 1975). Many of these species reach the limits of their range in Montana and should be considered of peripheral status; available information on many species is such that their status is undetermined, while other species have experienced population declines to various degrees and have been recognized by the U.S. Department of the Interior. Of the species noted, the desert cottontail, golden eagle, marsh hawk, prairie falcon, yellow-billed cuckoo and western kingbird have been observed in the Project Area.
The Smithsonian report to Congress (Smithsonian, 1975) lists ten plant species occuring in Montana which are considered either to be Endangered or Threatened. These species and their categories are as follows:
